A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OSI research work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original probing experiments, object-omission and attribute-neglect evaluations, qualitative examples and ablations, including additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original probing experiments, benchmark evaluations and ablations on FLUX.1-Dev and SD3.5-Medium, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: The probing procedure and OSI intervention remain unchanged: omission-minus-presence mean directions, normalization, key-vector shifts, top-ranked head selection and the intervention window are identical in Section 4 and Equations 5–7.

E1.justification: Both versions use GenEval two-object prompts, constructed three-to-six-object prompts and the non-spatial and attribute-binding subsets of T2I-CompBench. The probing datasets and appendix task coverage are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the base models and TACA for both backbones, with PLADIS evaluated only on FLUX. Comparator membership in the main and appendix experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain 30 inference steps, guidance scales of 3.5 for FLUX and 7.0 for SD3.5, and intervention during the first 15 steps. Dataset splits, labeling procedures, metrics and ablation protocols also match.

E4.justification: The direction, head-selection, token-specific, hyperparameter and intervention-duration ablations are retained unchanged. Appendices B–F preserve the encoder/head analyses, intervention-target study, distribution-mismatch analysis and time-dependent steering comparisons.

E5.justification: The same probe box plots and median/interquartile-range summaries remain in Figures 3–4. Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains the FLUX OSI GenEval average of 0.61, and Table 5 retains omitted-object accuracy of 0.70 for OSI-Omitted.

T1.justification: The flow-matching equations, probing-dataset definitions and mathematical formulation of OSI are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about detectable omission information, OSI's intervention mechanism and mitigation of object omission and attribute neglect. The added code-access sentence does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of token-specific effects, transfer to attributes and weaker SD3.5 probing remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the over-generation and ambiguous-concept limitations, while Appendix F preserves the same explanations of early intervention and time-insensitive steering.

D1.justification: The v3 abstract adds an explicit GitHub link for OSI code, which v1 lacks. Implementation settings and appendix construction/extraction instructions remain unchanged; the PDFs establish added access information but do not verify the repository's contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and reference list are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same positioning relative to earlier attention-guidance, text-embedding and MM-DiT alignment methods.

P1.justification: v3 adds the code-availability sentence and revises the funding acknowledgements. The scientific prose, terminology and section sequence otherwise remain unchanged, with text reflow across columns and pages.

P2.justification: Table 5 moves between columns on page 8, and Table 6 moves from page 8 to page 9. Table 1 is repositioned, and Tables A4–A5 gain bold headers and row labels. Figures and displayed scientific content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new code link supplies implementation-access information missing from v1, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Table formatting receives small refinements, while the scientific evidence, claims and limitations remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.
